name: Cable Lateral Raise (Cable Behind Glutes)
description: The cable lateral raise with the cable passing behind the glutes positions the cable at the low-back or glute level before the lift, changing the angle of resistance throughout the raise. This positioning maintains lateral deltoid tension through the bottom portion of the movement — where dumbbell raises have minimal tension — making it mechanically advantageous for complete medial deltoid loading across the full range.

execution.starting_position: Stand side-on to a low cable pulley. Reach behind the body and grasp the cable handle with the far hand, so the cable passes behind the glutes. Stand tall.
execution.setup_instructions: The cable should run behind the lower back and under the opposite arm's side. Grip the handle with the arm that is furthest from the cable stack.
steps: Step 1: Begin with the cable behind the glutes, arm at the side.
Step 2: Raise the working arm out to the side and upward to shoulder height.
Step 3: The cable will pull from behind — this unique angle provides early-range tension.
Step 5: Complete all reps then turn and repeat on the other side.
common_mistakes: Not actually passing the cable behind the glutes — the cable must run behind the body
Excessive lean toward the cable — maintain upright posture
safety_considerations: Light loads — this is a finisher or detail exercise, not a strength builder
Ensure cable attachment does not catch on clothing
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arm at side to shoulder height.
coaching_cues: Cable runs behind your back — not to the side
Lead with the elbow, not the hand
Feel the tension from the very bottom of the movement
